body.statement: For every \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\), the \((X,Z)\)-marginal of \(P^{\circ}\) is absolutely continuous with density bounded and strictly positive on each of its two support rectangles, while observed outcomes are bounded, exact stayers have probability zero, and marginal quasi-stayers exist. Conditional quasi-stayer support fails for every \(x\in[-1,0)\), a baseline region of probability \(p_{\circ}\). The observed objects are \(X_0=[-1,1]\), \(H=[-1,0]\times[1/2,1]\cup[0,1]\times[-1/4,1/4]\), \(g=0\), \(A=(1+5p_{\circ})/8\), \(T=0\), and \(d\nu_P(x)=p_{\circ}\mathbf 1\{x\in[-1,0]\}dx\). The obstacle envelopes equal \(r_P(x)=-\ell_P(x)=\min\{-x,1/2\}\) on \([-1,0]\) and vanish on \([0,1]\), yielding \(\Theta(P^{\circ})=[-3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ}),3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ})]\). The displayed affine laws \(Q_+^{\circ}\) and \(Q_-^{\circ}\) both belong to the continuous-trend legal completion class, preserve the entire observed law, and satisfy parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support and the stronger all-\(I\) equality because their period differences are respectively \(u_+^{\circ}(X)\) and \(u_-^{\circ}(X)\) at every dose. They satisfy the new conditional mean-movement bound and attain respectively \(-3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ})\) and \(3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ})\).
body.justification: The positive-density family proves that the conditional-support failure and non-singleton frontier persist away from atomic examples, while the two schedules display legal full-law attainment.
body.gap: The public conditional-quasi-stayer theorem covers the nested singleton regime, and the common-zero-baseline result has scalar geometry; neither supplies an absolutely continuous heterogeneous-baseline support-hole family with two observed-law-equivalent WAOSS values.
body.consumer: The family is a regular stress test for support diagnostics, obstacle solvers, and sensitivity plots indexed by the mass \(p_{\circ}\) of unsupported baselines.
body.proof_tex:
The two rectangles in the definition have respective areas \(1/2\) and \(1/2\).  Their density integrals are \(p_{\circ}\) and \(1-p_{\circ}\), so they define a probability law.  Since \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\), the density is bounded and strictly positive on each support rectangle.  The outcomes are zero, exact stayers form a Lebesgue-null set, and the second rectangle gives positive probability to every set \(\{|Z|\leq\eta\}\) with \(\eta>0\).  For each \(x\in[-1,0)\), however, the conditional support is \([1/2,1]\), so conditional quasi-stayers fail there.  Integrating the first rectangle over \(z\) shows that this baseline region has probability \(p_{\circ}\).

The definitions immediately yield
\[
X_0=[-1,1],
\qquad
H=[-1,0]\times[1/2,1]\ \cup\ [0,1]\times[-1/4,1/4],
\qquad
g=0,
\qquad
T=0.
\]
On the first rectangle \(S=1\); on the second, the conditional distribution of \(Z\) is symmetric.  Hence
\[
d\nu_P(x)=p_{\circ}\mathbf 1\{x\in[-1,0]\}\,dx.
\]
Moreover,
\[
A=p_{\circ}E[Z\mid Z\in[1/2,1]]
+(1-p_{\circ})E[|Z|\mid Z\in[-1/4,1/4]]
=\frac{3p_{\circ}}4+\frac{1-p_{\circ}}8
=\frac{1+5p_{\circ}}8.
\]

For \(x\in[0,1]\), the support contains \((x,0)\), so the cone at zero forces both obstacles to equal zero.  For \(x\in[-1,0]\), the local smallest change gives \(|u(x)|\leq1/2\), while the one-Lipschitz connection to \(u(0)=0\) gives \(|u(x)|\leq-x\).  Substitution in the envelope formulas shows these are the only restrictions:
\[
r_P(x)=-\ell_P(x)=
\begin{cases}
\min\{-x,1/2\},&x\in[-1,0],\\
0,&x\in[0,1].
\end{cases}
\]
Both envelope functions are feasible.  Therefore the extrema of the signed objective are
\[
V_P^{\pm}=\mathbin{\pm}p_{\circ}\int_{-1}^0\min\{-x,1/2\}\,dx
=\mathbin{\pm}\frac{3p_{\circ}}8,
\]
with the usual convention that \(V_P^+\) takes the plus sign.  The attained-interval formula now gives
\[
\Theta(P^{\circ})
=\left[-\frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
          \frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}\right].
\]

For \(s\in\{+,-\}\), evaluation of the displayed schedules at observed doses gives
\[
Y_1^{Q_s^{\circ}}(D_1)=0,
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_s^{\circ}}(D_2)=0,
\]
so the entire observed law is preserved.  Their difference is, for every \(d\in[-2,2]\),
\[
Y_2^{Q_s^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_s^{\circ}}(d)=u_s^{\circ}(X).
\]
This proves both baseline-support and all-\(I\) parallel trends and gives \(m_{Q_s^{\circ}}=u_s^{\circ}\).  The functions are bounded and one-Lipschitz.  Also \(|u_s^{\circ}(X)|\leq|Z|\) on both rectangles, so the common schedule slope has magnitude at most one and the conditional movement bound holds.  Thus both laws are legal.  Finally,
\[
\theta(Q_+^{\circ})=-\frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
\qquad
\theta(Q_-^{\circ})=\frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
\]
as asserted.
